Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Surendra Kumar

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Narendra Kumar Singh Hon'ble Mrs. Saroj Yadav,J. 
The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the accused/ applicant in Case Crime No.13 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 504, 506, 376-D I.P.C. and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Amritpur, District Farrukhabad with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
Heard Shri Surendra Kumar, learned counsel for the accused/ applicant, Shri Narendra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the complainant and learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State respondent.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the accused/applicant that the accused/applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has made no allegation of rape against any of the accused.
The victim refused to undergo medico-legal examination and the said fact has been noted by the doctor concerned in report, which is available on record as Annexure No.4.
He further submitted that the co accused Adesh Kumar who has been assigned the similar role, has already been granted bail by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 23.12.2022.
The applicant is in jail since 10.2.2022.

sentences.text: the applicant is on better footing, as such, the accused/ applicant should also be released on bail on the ground of parity.

Learned counsel for the complainant submitted that the bail application of the co accused Sonu @
Ajay Kumar is still pending, hence the present bail application should be rejected.

Learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State opposed the bail application of the accused/
applicant but did not dispute the parity.
Considered the rival submissions made by the parties' counsel and perused the record.

It transpires from the record that the victim has not levelled any allegation of rape against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. She refused to undergo medico- legal examination.
Co accused Adesh Kumar has already been granted bail by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the accused/ applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application filed on behalf of applicant is allowed.

Let the applicant - Jaiki Verma involved in Case Crime No.13 of 2022 (supra) be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to Jaiki Verma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72958169/
